title: feat(ai): add a provider abstraction and registry
problem: There is a single offline assistant and no way to register an alternative provider cleanly.
why: A registry keeps the optional layer extensible without coupling to any vendor.
scope: Define a provider factory keyed by name and resolve it from configuration, failing closed for unknown names.
guidance: Keep providers feature-gated and out of the default build.
tests: Unit tests with a mock provider
security: Providers cannot enable network access implicitly.

title: feat(ai): validate provider responses against a schema
problem: Model output could contain fabricated findings or locations if accepted unchecked.
why: The deterministic engine is authoritative; provider text must never introduce findings.
scope: Require provider output to be explanation-only and reject any payload that references locations or findings not already reported.
guidance: Constrain the provider interface to return only explanation text; validate and sanitize before display.
acceptance: Malformed or overreaching responses are rejected
tests: Unit tests with hostile mock responses
security: Central guarantee for the AI layer.

title: feat(ai): add rate limiting and backoff for providers
problem: A provider could be called once per finding, causing excessive requests and cost.
why: Limits keep the optional layer predictable and courteous.
scope: Add a configurable request budget, backoff, and clear diagnostics when the limit is reached.
guidance: Never retry indefinitely; fail closed and continue without assistance.
acceptance: Scan completes when the budget is exhausted
tests: Unit tests with a counting mock provider
security: Prevents accidental data exfiltration at scale.

title: docs(ai): document provider data flow and privacy
problem: It is not documented exactly what data leaves the machine when a provider is enabled.
why: Users must be able to make an informed consent decision.
scope: Document the exact payload shape, what is excluded (whole files, secrets), retention caveats, and how to keep everything offline.
guidance: Reference the network policy in the security model.
acceptance: Privacy section merged and linked from the AI guide

title: test(ai): guarantee deterministic offline fallback behavior
problem: The offline guidance path must provably work with assistance disabled and with providers unavailable.
why: The core scanner must never depend on assistance.
scope: Add tests asserting identical deterministic scans with assistance off, enabled-but-unavailable, and provider errors.
guidance: Assert findings and exit codes are unchanged in every case.
acceptance: Fallback tests cover all failure modes
tests: Unit and CLI tests with a failing mock provider

title: feat(ai): add safe model configuration defaults
problem: Model parameters (temperature, token limits) are not configurable, and unsafe values are not prevented.
why: Sensible bounds reduce nondeterminism and runaway cost.
scope: Add documented configuration with conservative defaults and validation bounds.
guidance: Reject out-of-range values during config validation.
acceptance: Defaults and bounds documented and tested

title: feat(ai): add provider failure handling and a circuit breaker
problem: Repeated provider failures would otherwise be retried for every finding, slowing scans.
why: A circuit breaker keeps scans fast and predictable under provider outages.
scope: After a configurable number of failures, disable assistance for the remainder of the run and record a diagnostic.
guidance: Fail closed and never block the deterministic result.
tests: Unit tests with an always-failing mock provider
